approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package that replaces the Motor Vehicle Standards Act 1989 with the Road Vehicle Standards Bill 2018 as the main law for regulating road vehicle imports and supply.

It allows the Commonwealth to impose cost-recovery charges on activities related to administering the Road Vehicle Standards Bill, specifically where those charges are a duty of customs under section 55 of the Constitution.
The bill does not set the charge amounts; these will be set in regulations that Parliament can disallow, allowing the relevant minister to consult stakeholders and make timely adjustments.
Replaces the Motor Vehicle Standards Act 1989 with the Road Vehicle Standards Bill 2018.
Allows the Commonwealth to impose cost-recovery charges for administering the Road Vehicle Standards Bill.
Ensures charges that are duties of customs are covered by this bill.
Leaves charge amounts to be set in disallowable regulations.
Allows the minister to consult stakeholders on charge amounts.
The Commonwealth, the relevant minister, stakeholders, and consumers using the Road Vehicle Standards Bill.

The Road Vehicle Standards Charges (Imposition-General) Bill 2018 was moved for a second reading, imposing charges to recover costs for regulating the first provision of road vehicles to the Australian market, with charges capped at no more than the Commonwealth's administrative costs.

The Road Vehicle Standards Charges (Imposition-Customs) Bill 2018 was moved for a second reading, imposing charges to recover costs for regulating first-provision road vehicles in Australia, with charges capped at the Commonwealth's administrative costs.

The Road Vehicle Standards Charges (Imposition-Excise) Bill 2018 was moved for a second reading, imposing charges for regulatory administration of the Road Vehicles Standards Bill 2018 and enabling cost recovery, with charges not set above the Commonwealth's likely costs.

Labor supported the Road Vehicle Standards package, which replaces the Motor Vehicle Standards Act, creates an online register of approved vehicles, and is projected to reduce industry compliance costs by $68 million, while noting stakeholder concerns about impacts on small workshops and campervan converters.

The Road Vehicle Standards Bill 2018 and four companion bills were presented as a modern framework for regulating road vehicles, projected to save industry an estimated $20 million, establish the Register of Approved Vehicles (saving around $14 million a year), and introduce compulsory recall powers. The government announced amendments to allow used-vehicle imports for campervan/motorhome conversions, adjust power-to-weight thresholds for specialist vehicles, permit left-hand-drive heavy vehicles, and presented addenda to the explanatory memoranda following the Scrutiny of Bills committee's recommendations.
